rv.q: All in all, Parcel from America is a nice bit of musical theatre with a great ensemble performance that is just the right fare for the holidays and ought to be extended through Christmas.

For those interested in a sincere human story that considers the impact of emigration, celebrates the importance of community, and brings to life the old Irish adage, “It is only in the shelter of our neighbors that we all can live,” this is a production that is sure to touch your heart.
Despite all its flaws, Parcel From America is impossible to hate.
Parcel From America stands out as a centering, mystical, and beautiful piece of theater.
It is a beautiful way to begin the Christmas season, offering a heartfelt reminder of the importance of community, delivered in a festive package of song, humor, and compassion.
This is a quiet, sentimental tale, a celebration of community support and unselfishness, and a new Christmas story that feels like it could take its place among all the familiar Yuletide classics.

cn.t: This heartwarming Irish musical about community and emigration in 1950s Ireland earns mostly positive reviews for its pitch-perfect storytelling, though one critic finds it disappointing despite the charming premise.
